standard.title: Initiate, sustain and extend exchanges
standard.description: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in a range of contexts, responding to ideas, opinions and perspectives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts, adjusting language in response to others and using persuasive and influencing language (AC9LCH8C01). They can summarise others' views and manage real-time language adjustment. They have not yet extended exchanges into wider community and issue-based contexts, used analytical language to evaluate rules and regulations, or communicated in formal contexts such as phone calls, official enquiries, or advocacy writing.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in a range of contexts — including community issues, formal communication, and advocacy — responding analytically to ideas, opinions and perspectives.

nodes.label: Extending exchanges into wider community and issue contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges about issues beyond personal experience — community, social, or global topics — using language appropriate to the scope of the discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate and sustain an exchange about a community or issue-based topic for at least six turns, using at least two analytical or evaluative language structures.
nodes.typical_width: Initiate conversations about wider community and social issues — including global topics; use analytical language to discuss and evaluate rules, policies and social questions; sustain communications across diverse contexts including meetings and extended discussions; deal with potential conflicts productively.
wider: Participate in a structured debate or formal discussion on a community issue — sustain a reasoned position under challenge, using evidence and analytical language
Compare how issue-based discussion is conducted in target language community contexts with Australian conventions — identify differences in how authority, evidence and disagreement are managed
nodes.hinge_reason: Extension into wider community and issue contexts is the defining expansion from Y7-8 exchanges. Students who can only sustain personal topic exchanges cannot meet the analytical and advocacy demands of the remaining Y9-10 descriptors.

response_modes.reason: Analytical and issue-based exchange language requires a growing repertoire of structures across different topic types and positions. Repeated engagement with varied community and social issues builds the flexible analytical vocabulary and argumentation capacity needed.

success_criteria: Initiates and sustains an issue-based exchange for at least six turns
Uses at least two analytical or evaluative language structures during the exchange

nodes.label: Formal communication contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can communicate in formal contexts — phone calls, official meetings, formal written enquiries — using appropriate register, structure and language for each context.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in or produce at least one formal communication (phone call simulation, formal meeting contribution, or formal written enquiry) using appropriate register throughout.
nodes.typical_width: Sustain communication in formal contexts — meetings, phone calls, official enquiries; use formal register and appropriate structural conventions; confirm understanding and request clarification in formal contexts; write to different audiences addressing real-life issues such as visa applications or scholarship enquiries.
wider: Compare formal communication conventions in the target language with Australian English equivalents — identify differences in register, structure, opening and closing conventions
Draft a formal written communication on a real issue of personal relevance — apply target language formal register and structural conventions appropriately

response_modes.reason: Formal communication contexts require students to understand what makes formal register different from informal, and to apply this consistently. Explicit register analysis of model formal texts, followed by structured production practice, builds the contextual awareness that formal communication demands.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Formal target language communication skills have direct practical value for background learners who may interact with target language institutions, family connections, or professional contexts. Width investment here builds capability with genuine real-world application.
success_criteria: Participates in or produces a formal communication using appropriate register throughout
Uses at least two formal register conventions appropriate to the communication context

nodes.label: Advocacy and conflict management in exchanges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can advocate for a position, address conflicting views, and use digital platforms to express concerns and contribute to wider community discussions.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one advocacy communication (written or spoken) addressing a real or realistic issue, using at least three argumentative or persuasive structures.
nodes.typical_width: Contribute to discussions dealing with potential conflicts; use digital resources to express concerns, make enquiries or advocate on issues; promote positions using analytical language; contribute thoughtfully to online forums and community discussions; write to different audiences on real-life issues.
wider: Produce a campaign or advocacy piece on a community issue — targeting a specific audience and using the persuasive and formal structures appropriate to that audience
Participate in a simulation of a formal meeting or community forum where positions conflict — manage the conflict productively using target language

response_modes.reason: Advocacy and conflict management integrates issue-based exchange skills (node 1) and formal communication capacity (node 2) into the highest-stakes interaction context. The teaching investment is in creating genuine advocacy conditions — real issues, real or realistic audiences — that require authentic persuasive engagement.

success_criteria: Produces an advocacy communication using at least three argumentative or persuasive structures
The communication is directed at a specific audience with appropriate register and format
